LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 11.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.1: Listening and speaking 11.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and speaking 11.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Strand 11 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How do facial expressions and gestures help us to communicate well? 2. Why should we listen actively to what others are saying?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen attentively to an audio recording with the sounds /aʊ/ /ð/ /θ/ and consonant cluster ‘sk’,

2. repeat words with the sounds /aʊ/ /ð/ /θ/ and consonant cluster ‘sk’ after the teacher or audio recordings accurately,

3. make a three-minute speech using vocabulary related to the theme,

4. recite poems about games, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen attentively to an audio recording with the sounds /aʊ/ /ð/ /θ/ and consonant cluster ‘sk’,
2. repeat words with the sounds /aʊ/ /ð/ /θ/ and consonant cluster ‘sk’ after the teacher or audio recordings accurately,
3. make a three-minute speech using vocabulary related to the theme,
4. recite poems about games, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and speaking 11.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: This is enhanced when the learner engages in activities such as giving a speech using non- verbal cues.

• Self-efficacy: This is realised when the learner ably interprets the nonverbal cues used by peers in communication.

Values:
Social Justice is encouraged as the learner accords equal opportunities and shares resources equitably while they watch and

give a speech about sports.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Effective Communication skills: These skills are developed as the learner engages in activities such as giving brief

speeches.

• Peer Education and Career Guidance: These are enhanced as the learner participates in making speeches in club meetings

as well as sporting activities.

Link to other Learning Areas:

• The learner applies the skill of listening in all learning areas.

• The learner also relates the content gained in listening to speeches on sports in learning of similar content in Creative

Arts.
